understanding: The task is to study the existing audit system (comprising static snapshots, deep LLM-agent chains, intake gates, and maintenance scheduling) and design a durable plan to improve its efficiency—defined as the share of real problems that are identified, survive filtering, and ultimately get fixed. The work must operate in DISCUSS mode, fix/strengthen existing mechanisms without introducing new ones, and produce a reviewable decomposition addressing six known pain points: deep-agent failures, coverage gaps, false-positive/miss tradeoffs, speed/window constraints, finding staleness, and fix reachability.
summary: Proposal decomposes the audit pipeline into four layers (Collection, Analysis, Intake, Remediation) and identifies efficiency losses at each. Root causes for the six known pains are traced to specific code/configuration weaknesses. The plan prioritizes fixes that strengthen existing PowerShell modules: hardening deep-agent subprocess lifecycle, expanding static coverage via existing snapshot providers, tuning intake-gate similarity thresholds with feedback loops, time-boxing audit windows, adding staleness metadata to findings, and instrumenting a lightweight fix-outcome tracker. All improvements reuse current scripts and data flows, avoiding new mechanisms per Foundation #2.

decision_atoms.statement: Fix deep-agent subprocess/job layer by adding a watchdog timeout and forced socket cleanup in Stop-Job, reusing existing job infrastructure in deep-audit-agent.ps1.
decision_atoms.reason: Root cause of deep:deep_failed is that hung LLM sockets survive Stop-Job, blocking subsequent agents. A timeout-kill pattern directly addresses this without new modules.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Aggressive socket cleanup may occasionally kill a slow-but-valid agent, losing a finding. Mitigated by a two-phase timeout (soft cancel, then hard kill) already partially present in the codebase.

decision_atoms.statement: Expand audit coverage by extending Get-AuditorSnapshot to include currently unmonitored assets (e.g., scheduled tasks, certificate store, DNS records) using existing WMI/registry providers already in lib/auditor.ps1.
decision_atoms.reason: Coverage gaps exist because snapshot providers are not exhaustive. Adding queries to existing cmdlets is a low-risk extension, not a new mechanism.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Broader snapshots increase runtime and data volume, potentially stressing the audit window. Mitigated by making new providers optional and window-aware.

decision_atoms.statement: Tune Invoke-BacklogIntakeGate similarity thresholds using a feedback loop that compares deduplication decisions against operator overrides, stored in the existing backlog-workpack.ps1 metadata.
decision_atoms.reason: False positives and misses stem from static similarity thresholds. A feedback loop adjusts thresholds based on operator corrections, improving precision/recall without new infrastructure.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires operators to consistently log overrides for the loop to be effective; initial weeks may see noisy adjustments. Acceptable given existing override logging.

decision_atoms.statement: Enforce a strict time-box in Start-AuditIfDue by adding a configurable hard-stop parameter that terminates the audit chain and flushes partial results, reusing the existing maintenance window logic.
decision_atoms.reason: Speed/window pain arises when audits overrun the 01-06 window, delaying maintenance. A hard-stop ensures the system remains predictable without new scheduling mechanisms.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Partial deep-audit results may be lost if the window expires mid-chain. Mitigated by checkpointing agent outputs to disk, a pattern already in audit.ps1.

decision_atoms.statement: Add a 'staleness' metadata field to findings in the backlog, updated by a lightweight daily job that compares finding timestamps against current system state using existing snapshot diff logic.
decision_atoms.reason: Outdated findings waste remediation effort. A staleness flag allows operators to filter or re-verify old findings, reusing the diff engine already in auditor.ps1.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Daily re-diffing adds compute load. Mitigated by limiting staleness checks to findings older than N days and using incremental snapshots.

decision_atoms.statement: Instrument a fix-outcome tracker in the findings→backlog→approved pipeline by adding a 'fix_status' field and a weekly summary report, leveraging existing backlog-workpack.ps1 export functions.
decision_atoms.reason: Reachability to fix is unmeasured. A simple status field (open/in-progress/fixed/dropped) with a report closes the loop, enabling measurement of the core efficiency metric without new systems.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Relies on operator discipline to update statuses. Mitigated by auto-detecting closure when a finding's snapshot diff disappears in subsequent audits.

assumptions: The existing PowerShell modules (lib/auditor.ps1, deep-audit-agent.ps1, audit.ps1, lib/backlog-workpack.ps1, driver/10-maintenance.ps1) are functional and can be modified in-place.
Operators will participate in the feedback loop by logging overrides and updating fix statuses, at least minimally.
The 01-06 maintenance window is a soft constraint that can be enforced programmatically without breaking other scheduled tasks.
LLM agent failures are primarily due to subprocess/socket management, not API rate limits or model unavailability.
The existing deduplication logic in Invoke-BacklogIntakeGate uses configurable similarity thresholds that can be adjusted dynamically.

risks.risk: Deep-agent socket cleanup may introduce instability if the forced kill corrupts shared state in audit.ps1.
risks.mitigation: Implement cleanup within a try/finally block scoped to the agent's job; test in a staging environment with simulated hung sockets before production rollout.

risks.risk: Expanded snapshot coverage significantly increases audit runtime, causing consistent window overruns.
risks.mitigation: Gate new providers behind a -Comprehensive switch; default to current coverage; monitor runtime in the first week and adjust hard-stop accordingly.

risks.risk: Feedback-loop threshold tuning may oscillate if operator overrides are inconsistent or sparse.
risks.mitigation: Use a dampened adjustment (exponential moving average) and require a minimum number of overrides before applying changes.

risks.risk: Staleness re-diffing may produce false staleness flags if the system state changes legitimately but the finding remains valid.
risks.mitigation: Staleness is advisory, not auto-closing; operators confirm before dropping. The diff logic will include a 'context match' tolerance.

minimal_version: Fix deep-agent subprocess lifecycle (decision_atom 1) and add fix-outcome tracker (decision_atom 6). These two changes directly address the core efficiency metric (real problems fixed) and the most acute failure mode (deep:deep_failed). Deploy in one maintenance cycle, measure fix-rate delta.
advanced_version: Implement all six decision_atoms in phased order: (1) deep-agent fix, (2) coverage expansion, (3) intake-gate tuning, (4) window hard-stop, (5) staleness metadata, (6) fix-outcome tracker. Each phase includes a one-week observation period with rollback points. The full plan transforms the audit pipeline into a measured, closed-loop system while staying within Foundation #2 constraints.
